subject: Erase proofing and operational handoff — DPA residency & deletion QA
messages:
From: Katie Olsen <katie.olsen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on deletion proof & backup retention (DPA)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this back for us. As part of Nimbus Health's DPA review we need more detail on how Redwood will provide operational proof of deletion and how backups / snapshots are handled across regions. A few concrete asks from Legal + Security: 

- What constitutes a "proof of deletion" (manifest, checksum, signed attestation)?
- How do you handle backups/snapshots that may contain a customer's data (primary + secondary replicas)?
- Can you provide a certified manifest with a signature we can verify (we prefer something signed by a KMS-backed key)?
- What are the expected timelines for full deletion (including backups) after a termination request?
- How is legal hold handled if a court asks to preserve data?

We've attached our redline-friendly questionnaire (pdf) and would like a short runbook we can reference in the DPA appendix. Can we get a first-pass reply today and schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your ops team?

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Olsen
Head of Security Programs | Nimbus Health
katie.olsen@nimbushealth.com

Attachments: nimbus_dpa_questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Katie Olsen <katie.olsen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & backup retention (DPA)

Katie —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by what we can provide as artifacts and an ops handshake: 

- Proof of deletion: We produce an erase manifest (CSV) that enumerates object ids/timestamps and a SHA256 checksum per object, plus a signed attestation signed by a KMS key (key-id: redwood-erase-prod). We can also provide a PDF certificate of erasure.

- Backups & snapshots: Primary data is marked for immediate tombstone; snapshots are handled by a staged purge. For production primary data we aim to remove access immediately and mark objects for deletion. Snapshots and cross-region replicas follow a separate TTL purge depending on the snapshot tier (see below).

- Signed attestation: yes, KMS-backed signatures are standard for this workflow. We can provide verification instructions.

- Timeline: Our default SLO is: primary erase acknowledgement within 7 days (attestation + manifest), full wipe including standard backups within 45 days. We can discuss a shorter window for primary-only purge.

- Legal hold: We will not perform a destructive purge if a verified legal hold is in place; we support on-demand preservation after a formal request from legal with contact point and ticket reference.

Artifacts we can hand over (examples attached):
- erase_playbook_v1.pdf: operational runbook for erase operations
- erase_manifest_template.csv: example manifest (object id, path, deleted_at, checksum, signer, signature)
- dpa_redlines_nimbus_v2.docx: proposed redline language that matches the runbook and SLOs

Operational handshake: we propose an automated ticket (Jira INF-4821) created at erase initiation, a webhook to your security queue when primary objects are tombstoned, and a final S3-stored manifest + signed attestation once background snapshot purges complete.

If you want, Ben can walk through the exact purge lifecycle with your ops folks tomorrow. Happy to set up 30 minutes.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: erase_playbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf), erase_manifest_template.csv (text/csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Katie Olsen <katie.olsen@nimbushealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & backup retention (DPA)

Katie / team —

Adding a bit more technical color on the end-to-end flow so your engineering/legal ops get comfortable with the evidence chain: 

1) Tombstone primary objects: immediate mark and remove from active index. This action triggers an erase ticket (INF-4821) and a webhook payload with object ids.
2) Emit erase manifest: a CSV with columns (object_id, storage_path, deleted_at_utc, sha256, signer, signature_b64). The signature is produced by the redwood-erase-prod KMS key; verification instructions included in the runbook.
3) Snapshot purge: snapshots are tiered. Hot snapshots (replicas within the same region) are eligible for purge on a 30–45 day window; cold snapshots (cross-region archival) are purged on a 60–90 day cadence depending on retention tier. Note: we can compress that range if it's a contractual must.
4) Backup verification: after the purge sweep runs we produce a final manifest and a signed certificate of erasure that references the original erase ticket and manifest. That final CSV is stored in a locked S3 path and a reference is posted to the ticket.

Operational notes:
- KV cache and in-memory caches are cleared in-line at time of tombstone.
- For encrypted backups, we can also rotate/destroy the specific encryption envelope keys used for that tenant (subject to key escrow / legal hold constraints).
- We log all actions with trace ids for audit (trace id included in both initial and final manifests).

Please confirm whether the snapshot purge window above (30–45 / 60–90) meets Nimbus' expectations. I've attached a sample manifest template for your legal team to review.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: erase_manifest_template.csv (text/csv)

From: Katie Olsen <katie.olsen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & backup retention (DPA)

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple of follow-ups and a proposed change from Nimbus legal: 

- Our baseline requirement is that all backups containing customer data must be purged within 30 days of termination, including hot snapshots. The 45 / 60 windows would be a blocker for us unless we can get a contractual commitment to accelerate.
- We require the signed attestation to include the KMS key fingerprint and a verification URL or public key so our security team can validate signatures independently.
- Legal hold language: Nimbus will only submit legal hold requests via our Legal Ops mailbox and will provide the court order reference; we'd like Redwood to provide a defined SLA for responding to legal hold requests (acknowledge within 48 hours).

Can you confirm whether you can meet a strict 30-day window for all production backups? If that isn't possible, please state the minimum achievable window and the engineering effort & ETA to shorten it. Also attaching our minor redlines to your doc (see attached).

Best,
Katie

Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & backup retention (DPA)

Katie —

Thanks for the candid ask and for the redlines. I've pulled together an operational compromise we can commit to in the DPA and the implementation cadence if Nimbus approves: 

Proposed commitments (final):
- Primary production data: full tombstone and removal from active indexes immediately; initial erase manifest + KMS-signed attestation delivered within 7 calendar days.
- Production backups & hot snapshots: contractually committed purge within 30 calendar days. We will prioritize engineering work to guarantee 30 days for any snapshot tier marked as 'production' in the account metadata.
- Cold/cross-region archival copies: purge within 60 calendar days by default; if Nimbus requires 30 days for all copies we will need to scope additional operational changes (estimated 4–6 weeks of engineering work after contract signature).
- Legal hold: Redwood will acknowledge legal hold requests within 48 hours and suspend destructive actions for any ticket that has an active legal hold flag. We will require a formal request via Legal Ops and a ticket reference for audit.
- Evidence chain: initial manifest (CSV) and final manifest + PDF certificate will include KMS key id and fingerprint, trace ids, and a verification URL. Final artifacts stored on a locked S3 path and a DocuSign-ready certificate template available if you need an attested document for regulators.

Next steps:
1) If Nimbus accepts the above, Redwood will update the DPA redline (attached: dpa_redlines_nimbus_v2.docx) and push a DocuSign envelope.
2) Engineering will open a targeted project to shorten cold-copy purge windows to 30 days if that is required — estimate 4–6 weeks.
3) Schedule a 30-minute ops walk-through (Ben + Marissa + your infra ops) to validate the manifest format and signature verification flow.

Please reply with approval or any final feedback; happy to iterate.

— Laura Bennett
Group Product Lead, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
